findings.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client size check hardcodes 10MB for every type, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb/max_image_size_kb: sites with limits above 10MB now block legitimate uploads, and sites with lower attachment limits let users upload the whole file only to be rejected by the server.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Any logged-in user can post up to 10MB crafted images (decompression bombs) that trigger up to 5 unthrottled convert+ImageOptim passes each, pinning CPU and memory and blocking the per-process Scheduler::Defer queue; there is no rate limit, and this runs before Upload.create_for rejects anything.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — ImageMagick now runs on raw user-controlled bytes before Upload.create_for's authorized-extension and upload-permission validation; the gate is only the user-supplied filename extension, while convert picks the decoder from the file content (ImageTragick-class exposure).

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — downsize's false return is never checked, so a failing convert (corrupt or non-image file named .jpg, OOM on a bomb, rejected gifsicle args) is retried 5 identical times and the original oversized file is then passed to Upload.create_for without any log or signal.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:137 — When allow_animated_thumbnails is on, a .gif path goes to gifsicle with "--resize-fit 80%", which is not valid WxH geometry, so oversized animated GIFs never shrink and just burn 5 failed passes.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:129 — When allow_animated_thumbnails is off (or the tempfile path lacks .gif), the new original-upload downsize runs convert on from[0], silently replacing an animated GIF with a static first frame.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — The second def self.downsize silently shadows the 5-arg (w,h) version: any existing downsize(from,to,w,h,opts) caller now raises ArgumentError, 4-arg calls pass an Integer as opts and raise TypeError at opts[:allow_animation], and public OptimizedImage.dimensions was removed.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — ImageOptim atomically replaces the file at the path (new inode), so the open Tempfile's size stays frozen at the pass-1 output; the loop can over-shrink through all 5 passes, and create_for records a filesize that does not match the stored file.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — The API URL download is hardcoded to 10.megabytes regardless of site settings; a larger file makes download fail and get rescued to nil, then line 72 calls tempfile.size on nil (500 when sync, silent swallowed failure with no MessageBus reply when deferred).

app/models/optimized_image.rb:161 — convert_with interpolates tempfile.path unescaped into a backtick shell, and the new call site feeds it a path whose URL-download prefix includes user-controlled params[:type] ("discourse-upload-#{type}"), which risks command injection for API callers.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 handler always reports a 10240 KB limit, which is tied to neither the web server's body-size limit that produced the 413 nor the admin's configured limits, so users are told the wrong maximum.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the 4-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` at line 145, so any existing width/height caller gets `max_height` bound to `opts` (TypeError on `opts[:allow_animation]`) or ArgumentError with 5 args.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — For GIFs with allow_animated_thumbnails on, "80%" goes to `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%` (via downsize_instructions_animated -> resize_instructions_animated), which only takes WxH, so every attempt fails and large animated GIFs are never shrunk.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — The loop checks `tempfile.size` (fstat on the open Tempfile fd), but ImageOptim#optimize_image! in convert_with replaces the path through a rename, so after the first pass the size is stale: the loop can run all 5 shrinks for nothing and pass a wrong filesize to Upload.create_for at line 72.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — The boolean from `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored, so a failed convert (e.g. a non-image file with an image extension) is retried 5 times with no logging and no early exit.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — When allow_animated_thumbnails is off, downsize_instructions reads `#{from}[0]`, so an oversized animated GIF is silently flattened to its first frame instead of being rejected.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The client-side size limit is hardcoded to 10MB for every upload type, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb and max_image_size_kb, so attachments or images the site allows above 10MB are now rejected in the browser.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 handler shows a hardcoded 10MB limit that has nothing to do with the web server's real request-size limit or the site settings, so users see a misleading error.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — The API URL download is capped at a hardcoded 10.megabytes instead of the site setting, so files over 10MB make FileHelper.download return nil and `tempfile.size` at line 72 raises NoMethodError on nil.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65 — Up to 5 sequential full-decode ImageMagick convert + ImageOptim passes run on every oversized upload, in the request for synchronous API calls and on the process's serial Scheduler::Defer queue otherwise; a 10MB JPEG decodes to hundreds of MB of pixel buffer per pass and holds up the worker/queue for seconds to minutes

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — A fixed "80%" step per pass cuts pixel area by only ~36% each time, so large inputs need several full re-encodes and can still exceed the limit after 5 passes (then get rejected and the work is thrown away); computing one scale factor from sqrt(max_size/actual_size) would need a single pass and avoid stacking lossy re-encodes

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — The loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize's false return value, so a failed convert or gifsicle run retries on the same input up to 5 times, each time spawning a new process that parses the whole file (up to 10MB)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:164 — convert_with runs the CPU-heavy ImageOptim lossless optimizer chain (optipng/pngcrush/advpng/jpegoptim etc.) after every intermediate downsize pass rather than once on the final output, multiplying the most expensive step by up to 5

app/models/optimized_image.rb:138 — For GIFs with allow_animated_thumbnails, the "80%" string is passed to gifsicle --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so every pass likely fails after parsing and coalescing the whole animated GIF; the result is 5 wasted gifsicle runs and a rejected upload

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Replacing the client check with a hardcoded 10MB for every upload type (attachments included) means files the server will reject by max_attachment_size_kb or max_image_size_kb are still fully uploaded, wasting bandwidth and worker time

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL uploads now always download up to 10MB whatever the type or site setting, including attachments that can't be downsized and will fail size validation, adding avoidable network I/O and temp-disk usage

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — tempfile.size is read from the open file descriptor; if ImageOptim swaps in the optimized file with a rename (new inode), the loop sees the stale size and always runs all 5 passes, and Upload.create_for gets the wrong filesize

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Loop condition reads Tempfile#size (fstat on the original fd), but ImageOptim.optimize_image! in convert_with replaces the path by atomic rename, so after pass 1 the size never changes; the loop always runs all 5 passes (over-shrinking to ~33% dimensions) and passes a stale size to Upload.create_for (verified with a Ruby Tempfile rename repro)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Up to 5 sequential ImageMagick convert + ImageOptim runs with no timeout or -limit resource cap now execute in the web process (synchronous API request or the shared Scheduler::Defer thread at line 19), so a 10MB image or a decompression-bomb PNG can hang or OOM the worker

app/models/optimized_image.rb:161 — convert_with runs `... &> /dev/null` through /bin/sh, and under dash (the Debian/Ubuntu default) that backgrounds convert and returns exit 0, so the new in-place loop starts overlapping convert/ImageOptim writers on the same tempfile path and can store a corrupted upload (verified that dash backgrounds it and returns status=0)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — The return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (false on failure) is ignored, so a deterministic convert failure is retried 5 times on a full-size image and the still-oversized file then goes to Upload.create_for, which fails with a generic too-large error after burning CPU

app/models/optimized_image.rb:138 — With allow_animated_thumbnails on, a .gif tempfile goes to resize_instructions_animated, which passes "80%" to gifsicle --resize-fit (it expects WxH), so every pass fails and oversized animated GIFs are never reduced

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — downsize is called with from == to, so a convert or ImageOptim killed or failing mid-write truncates the only copy of the upload; the smaller corrupt file then passes the size check and is stored, because the false return is ignored

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently discards the width/height version at line 145, so existing callers using (from, to, w, h[, opts]) now get an ArgumentError, or a TypeError from Integer#[] on opts (verified in Ruby; those callers are not in this 3-file snapshot)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The hardcoded 10MB client limit replaces max_<type>_size_kb for all types, so attachments above the server limit upload in full and then fail asynchronously over MessageBus, legitimately larger configured limits are blocked, and the 413 alert at line 246 reports a wrong limit

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — rescue nil` swallows download failures (and the hardcoded 10.megabytes cap now also ignores max_attachment_size_kb); the new nil guard at line 64 skips resizing but line 72 still calls tempfile.size on nil, so in the Defer path the client never gets a MessageBus reply

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — New downsize call feeds tempfile.path into the unescaped backtick shell in optimized_image.rb:161, and part of that path comes from the user: the API URL path uses the prefix "discourse-upload-#{params[:type]}", and multipart temp files take their extension from the user's filename, so shell metacharacters or a %0A newline can inject commands

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Any logged-in user can make the server run up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick convert runs plus ImageOptim passes on attacker-controlled bytes before any size or content validation, just by naming a file *.png/*.jpg; there is no rate limit, and it blocks the single Scheduler::Defer thread (or the request thread for synchronous API calls), so decompression bombs and incompressible images give a cheap CPU/memory DoS

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Whether ImageMagick runs is decided only by the user-supplied filename/URL-path extension (FileHelper.is_image?) and not by the content, so crafted payloads (MVG/MSL/SVG with url:/msl:/ephemeral coders, ImageTragick-style) reach convert, which sniffs magic bytes and ignores the extension; this exposes file read, SSRF, or RCE on unpatched ImageMagick without a restrictive policy.xml

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — URL downloads by API now use a hardcoded 10.megabytes cap instead of the admin-configured max_image_size_kb, and the same cap applies to attachments regardless of max_attachment_size_kb, so the server fetches and holds more attacker-chosen data than configured before validation

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63 — New auto-downsize loop ships with zero tests (diff touches no spec): shrink success, still-over-limit after 5 attempts, non-image skip, and max_image_size_kb=0 skip are all unverified

app/models/optimized_image.rb:145 — downsize is defined twice so the width/height form is silently dead (Ruby warns about the redefinition); verified downsize(from,to,w,h) now raises TypeError and downsize(from,to,w,h,opts) raises ArgumentError, and no spec pins either signature

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of downsize is ignored, so a convert/ImageOptim failure just loops 5 times and uploads the oversized file anyway; no test covers the failure path

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Animated GIF path is untested: allow_animation only applies when tempfile.path ends in .gif, otherwise downsize_instructions uses from[0] and flattens the GIF to one frame

app/models/optimized_image.rb:153 — optimize() arity changed (width,height -> dimensions string) and self.dimensions was removed with no spec updates or new assertions on the generated convert/gifsicle geometry for resize/downsize

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — validateUploadedFiles now hardcodes 10MB for every type (attachments too) instead of max_<type>_size_kb, a behavior change with no JS test added or updated for image vs attachment limits
app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — 413 error message now always reports a hardcoded 10240 KB, untested and inconsistent with the server-side max_image_size_kb

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes client-side and API-download size limits to a hardcoded 10MB (utilities.js and FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes)), and adds a pre-validation loop in uploads_controller.rb that can run up to 5 synchronous `OptimizedImage.downsize` passes while the tempfile is still oversized. `OptimizedImage.downsize` ultimately shells out via backticks in `convert_with`, so this can consume significant CPU/memory per request before `Upload.create_for` rejects/accepts. While the finding’s mention of Scheduler::Defer isn’t shown in the diff, the unthrottled multi-pass convert work on user-controlled images is directly introduced here and is a DoS/security risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — ImageMagick now runs on raw user-controlled bytes before Upload.create_for's authorized-extension and upload-permission validation; the gate is only the user-supplied filename extension, while convert picks the decoder from the file content (ImageTragick-class exposure).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a pre-processing loop in `create_upload` that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, ...)` (ImageMagick/convert) on the raw uploaded/downloaded tempfile *before* `Upload.create_for(...)` runs. The only gating shown is `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, where `filename` comes from `file.original_filename` or the URL basename—both user-controlled. This means ImageMagick is invoked on attacker-supplied bytes based on a user-supplied name/extension prior to any validation that might exist inside `Upload.create_for`, matching the finding’s concern about exposing ImageMagick to untrusted content.

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times but never checks its return value. From the diff, `OptimizedImage.downsize` delegates to `optimize` -> `convert_with`, which returns `false` on failure and otherwise returns `nil` (no success signal). If conversion fails (corrupt/non-image file with an image filename, resource failure, etc.), `tempfile.size` will remain unchanged, so the loop will retry the same failing operation 5 times and then proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` with an oversized/unmodified file, with no logging or error handling added here.

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in uploads_controller.rb downsizes the *original* uploaded image in-place (from==to) via `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. In optimized_image.rb, the `_animated` instruction path is only used when `opts[:allow_animation]` is truthy *and* the filename matches `/\.GIF$/i`; otherwise it will run the non-animated `downsize_instructions` even for GIFs. Given this runs in-place on the original tempfile, an animated GIF can be converted through the non-animated pipeline and lose animation (data loss). The finding’s specific mention of `from[0]` isn’t shown in this diff, but the diff does show the condition that would force animated GIFs down the non-animated path when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is off.

adjudication.rationale: In `create_upload`, the API URL path now does `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) rescue nil`. If the download raises (e.g., file exceeds that hard limit), `tempfile` becomes `nil`, but later the code unconditionally calls `tempfile.size` in `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)`, which would raise and 500. The added downsizing block guards with `if tempfile && ...`, but the final `tempfile.size` does not, so this failure mode is real and made more likely by hardcoding 10MB instead of the site setting.

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` unconditionally attempts to downsize any image (`FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`) that exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, and passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` into `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Up to 5 sequential ImageMagick convert + ImageOptim runs with no timeout or -limit resource cap now execute in the web process (synchronous API request or the shared Scheduler::Defer thread at line 19), so a 10MB image or a decompression-bomb PNG can hang or OOM the worker
